think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 30-year-old HIV-negative Chinese female presents with 8 months of fever, cough, and thoracic back pain with osteolytic destruction of the T6 vertebral body and lung consolidation, simulating spinal/pulmonary tuberculosis (Pott's disease) or bacterial spondylodiscitis. She failed a 6-month trial of anti-tuberculosis therapy and multiple broad-spectrum antibiotics, subsequently precipitating septic shock, while routine cultures and fungal biomarkers (beta-D-glucan, galactomannan, Cryptococcus antigen) remained negative.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The point of transfer and hospital admission triage (vitals, T5/T6 spine tenderness, baseline leukocytosis, anemia, elevated CRP/procalcitonin, and CT/PET imaging showing left upper lobe consolidation and T6 vertebral osteolytic lesion), immediately prior to empiric escalation, acute septic shock decompensation, invasive lung/bone biopsy, and mNGS.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pott's disease (spinal tuberculosis) is characterized by necrotizing granulomas with positive acid-fast staining or TB-PCR and responds to standard anti-tuberculous regimens; disseminated talaromycosis in HIV-negative patients frequently arises in the context of neutralizing anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies, presenting with osteolytic lesions, pulmonary involvement, and yeast forms inside macrophages identified on mNGS.
case_prompt:
A 30-year-old Chinese female was transferred to a tertiary hospital presenting with an 8-month history of persistent, irregular high fevers (temperatures up to 39.4 C) and cough, accompanied by progressive thoracic chest and back pain of 3 months' duration. She had no history of unprotected sex or blood transfusions, had no personal or family history of chronic illness, and denied travel outside her hometown over the preceding 10 years. Prior to transfer, she had undergone a 21-day course of intravenous cefoperazone-sulbactam without clinical response, followed by a 6-month empirical course of four-drug antimycobacterial therapy (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) with no symptomatic improvement and progressive worsening of back pain.

On initial admission physical examination, body temperature was 37.3 C, blood pressure was 107/74 mmHg, heart rate was 107 beats/min, and respiratory rate was 20 breaths/min. The physical examination was notable only for marked focal tenderness over the T5-T6 thoracic spinous processes.

Initial laboratory evaluation revealed a white blood cell count of 13.83 x 10^9/L with 95.4% neutrophils and 2.8% lymphocytes, hemoglobin of 77 g/L, and albumin of 35.9 g/L. Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated, including C-reactive protein of 112.0 mg/L, procalcitonin of 17.70 ng/mL, interleukin-6 of 26.40 pg/mL, and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 110 mm/h. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) serology was negative. Multiple peripheral blood cultures showed no microbial growth.

Chest computed tomography and 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed hypermetabolic consolidation, scattered patches, nodules, and ground-glass opacities with thickening of interlobular septa in the left upper pulmonary lobe, and hypometabolic osteolytic destruction involving the T6 thoracic vertebral body.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Strongly considered given chronic fever, lung consolidation, and destructive thoracic vertebral osteolysis; however, the patient failed a 6-month empirical trial of four-drug anti-tuberculosis therapy, and multiple PPD tests, interferon-gamma release assays, AFB smears, cultures, and tissue TB-qPCR assays were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Considering her symptoms and the imaging features (Figure 1A) observed in her chest CT, she was prescribed anti-tuberculosis treatment comprising isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol on December 15, 2021. She was non-responsive to the medications for up to six months.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute Bacterial Spondylodiscitis / Severe Community-Acquired Sepsis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Marked leukocytosis with 95.4% neutrophils, procalcitonin of 17.7 ng/mL, and vertebral destruction led to empiric intravenous piperacillin-sulbactam, levofloxacin, and meropenem; however, fevers persisted, blood cultures remained sterile, and she deteriorated into septic shock requiring vasopressors.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The possibility of bacterial infection was first considered based on the clinical characteristics and auxiliary examinations. The physician intravenously administered piperacillin-sulbactam and levofloxacin to the patient. However, the patient was feverish, with a maximum temperature of approximately 39 C.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Talaromycosis with Anti-Interferon-Gamma Autoantibodies
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Percutaneous lung biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with suspicious intracellular fungal elements on silver/PAS staining, followed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing detecting Talaromyces marneffei (confirmed by rDNA ITS PCR/sequencing) and detection of high-titer neutralizing anti-IFN-gamma autoantibodies (1:2500), with rapid defervescence on amphotericin B.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Eventually, we performed mNGS, which detected 1655 reads of Talaromyces spp. (Illumina NextSeq 550, Chengdu, China), including 1160 reads of T. marneffei, 435 reads of Human gamma herpesvirus 4 (EBV), no other bacteria and parasite had been detected.

editor_comments: Zero pathogen spoilers in prompt; admission breakpoint held prior to septic shock decompensation and mNGS biopsy. Verbatim quotes validated.
